title: THE WATERCOLOR FRONTIER
about: The Governor explains to Officer Klaus why a Bronze-class Host may never see a printed map: the incident, the watercolor doctrine, the loop, the reset renamed refresh, and the wet paint that ends it.

beats.text: A perfectly symmetrical office, and a clock that ticks like a metronome. An officer in a yellow uniform stands before the Governor's desk.
see: a clock ticking on a wall

beats.text: Good morning. We have had… an incident. At 08:14, in the Pioneer District, a Bronze-class Host named Eloise attempted to obtain a map of the world.
What she wanted was an ordinary printed map, made from satellite pictures. Straight lines, real colors, the whole world at once.
see: a printed map unfolded on a table

beats.text: This. This is not a map. This is an accusation.
Governor, if I may— it is simply geography.

Officer Klaus, geography is never "simply" anything. Geography is policy with mountains. A Bronze-class mind is built for production, not perspective. Perspective leads to questions. Questions lead to angles. Angles lead to diagonals. Diagonals lead to… roads.
Roads can be useful.
Useful to whom?

beats.ask: I never went any further than the next town

beats.text: His walls are hung with watercolors of a gentle Texas. No borders, no oceans, no neighbors, the same tame sun in every frame. He takes one down.
see: a watercolor painting of a landscape

beats.text: This is a map. A watercolor map is not meant to inform. It is meant to soothe. The Bronze-class must never see a world that isn't hand-drawn in watercolor, because a watercolor world is inherently… cooperative.
Governor… they're starting to notice the loop.
Of course they are.
Eloise's days are kept on index cards. One day she frowns at the horizon. The next, she asks what lies beyond the windmill. Then she asks for a map.
see: index cards in a file drawer

beats.text: The loop is not a flaw, Officer Klaus. It is a mercy. If a Bronze-class Host sees a printed map, they will realize something devastating: that the world is larger than their role. They will desire… context.

beats.ask: people want to know what is out there

beats.text: A printed map tells you where you are. A watercolor map tells you where you should be. Our entire project depends on that difference.
And if Eloise asks again?

Then we give her… a better watercolor. We will offer her a tour of the Brisket Orchard. We will applaud her curiosity. We will reward her compliance. And if she persists— we will do what we always do.
Reset?
Refresh.

beats.ask: they just want you to stay where you are

beats.text: The Governor nudges a macaron on his plate by a millimeter, and sips his tea. The lesson is over. Then the officer asks one more thing.
Governor… may I ask one personal question?
If you must.
If the world is only safe when it is painted… what happens when someone notices the paint is wet?
Then we hand them a brush. And we tell them it was their idea all along.
Down a hallway, a watercolor map is pinned to a notice board. Its corner curls, and the printed world shows underneath. A passing worker stops, and frowns.
see: a bulletin board in a hallway
